channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: When Public Health Loses the Public's Trust
item.description: Public trust is not lost all at once; it erodes through exaggeration, inconsistency and messages that do not match lived experience. In nicotine policy, that damage grows when adults are told to quit smoking but are denied clear, proportionate information about lower-risk alternatives. Once public health sounds more interested in control than honesty, people start looking elsewhere for answers. Rebuilding trust means being accurate about risk, transparent about uncertainty and respectful of the people policy is meant to help. (Published on August 28, 2026bydaily-pouch.com)

item.title: In defense of nicotine
item.description: Nicotine is usually discussed only as a problem, which leaves the public with a distorted picture of why people use it. Its potential upsides do not make it harmless or suitable for everyone, but they do help explain demand beyond addiction alone. The main public health failure comes from confusing nicotine with smoking. A more honest debate would separate the substance from combustion, acknowledge both risks and benefits, and focus policy on reducing the harms that actually kill. (Published on August 31, 2026bysubstack.com)

item.title: Australia’s Backwards Nicotine Policy Leaves Cigarettes Legal and Safer Alternatives Restricted
item.description: Australia’s nicotine policy has created a striking contradiction: cigarettes remain legal and easy to buy, while safer alternatives are pushed behind barriers many smokers cannot realistically navigate. That imbalance does not reduce harm; it protects the most dangerous product from meaningful competition. Adult smokers need regulated, accessible routes away from combustion, not a system that makes quitting harder than continuing. Public health policy should be judged by whether it helps people leave cigarettes behind. (Published on August 31, 2026byvapingpost.com)

item.title: Four Countries, Four Nicotine Futures
item.description: Four countries can tell four very different nicotine stories. Some make safer alternatives visible and accessible; others restrict them while cigarettes remain easy to buy; some lose control to illicit markets; others show how smoking can fall faster with a broader harm reduction approach. These are not abstract policy experiments — they shape what real smokers can actually do. The future of nicotine policy will depend on whether governments learn from outcomes or keep defending assumptions. (Published on August 31, 2026bysubstack.com)

item.title: Opinion: In Saskatchewan, I was too old to buy illegal nicotine pouches, and that should concern us
item.description: Saskatchewan’s nicotine pouch debate shows what happens when legal rules fail to match consumer reality. A product can be restricted on paper while still circulating through channels with weaker checks, less accountability and no clear path for adult smokers. That should concern anyone interested in youth protection or harm reduction. Regulation should bring smoke-free alternatives into a controlled market, not leave access to confusion, loopholes and illegal supply. (Published on August 31, 2026byleaderpost.com)
